extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational humor researchers and practitioners interested in sarcasm detection
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating a deep learning system to detect sarcasm in text using features from pop culture sarcasm corpora and English humor literature, and reporting training/validation performance and comparisons to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarcastic word distribution features
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually extract the sarcastic word distribution features of a benchmark pop culture sarcasm corpus, containing sarcastic dialogues and monologues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes manual extraction of sarcastic word distribution features from a benchmark pop-culture sarcasm corpus as an input feature source for the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input representation: weighted vectors / input sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: We generate input sequences formed of the weighted vectors from such words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature words are converted to weighted vectors and composed into input sequences for the model; the abstract presents this representation as the primary model input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model architecture: four parallel deep LSTM networks (pLSTM)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amalgamation of four parallel deep long-short term networks (pLSTM), each with distinctive activation classifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed architecture uses four parallel deep LSTM modules, each paired with a distinctive activation classifier; these parallel modules are the central design choice aimed at improving sarcasm detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objective: successful detection of sarcasm from text
rubrics_metrics.description: These modules are primarily aimed at successfully detecting sarcasm from the text corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stated goal of the architecture and feature pipeline is robust sarcasm detection across the supplied corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training accuracy as performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Our proposed model for detecting sarcasm peaks a training accuracy of 98.95% when trained with the discussed dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports peak training accuracy (98.95%) on the discussed training data as an indicator of model fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation accuracy on English humor literature
rubrics_metrics.description: It obtains the highest of 98.31% overall validation accuracy on two handpicked Project Gutenberg English humor literature among all the test cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation accuracy on two selected Project Gutenberg English humor texts (98.31%) is presented as an external validation/performance measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to prior work / state-of-the-art claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Our approach transcends previous state-of-the-art works on several sarcasm corpora and results in a new gold standard performance for sarcasm detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper claims to outperform previous state-of-the-art methods on several sarcasm corpora and to set a new gold-standard performance; this functions as an evaluative benchmark claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets used: benchmark pop culture sarcasm corpus and Project Gutenberg English humor literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The work uses a benchmark pop culture sarcasm corpus (sarcastic dialogues and monologues) and two handpicked Project Gutenberg English humor literature texts for validation/testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset selection (pop culture sarcasm corpus for training/feature extraction and Gutenberg humor texts for validation) is an explicit part of the experimental setup and influences reported performance.
